translation_notes: EX_A/EX_B/EX_C are hand-formatted SPARQL/N-Triples IRI TEXT (`"<http://example/a>"`, a str), spliced into the query with an f-string. That is precisely the pattern the strate targets, and translating it correctly is NOT a mechanical `s{ ASK { {EX_A} {EX_B} {EX_C} . } }` wrap around the untouched constants: coercion.md is explicit that a plain `str` becomes a PLAIN LITERAL (`f{"a"}.datatype is None`), so interpolating the string `"<http://example/a>"` as-is would silently bind `Literal('<http://example/a>')` -- a literal whose lexical form happens to look like an IRI -- never matching the graph's actual `URIRef('http://example/a')`. Verified this is a real, silent near-miss (not a raised error) by transpiling the naive version separately: the ASK evaluates to False with no diagnostic.

the fix is the one-line restructuring INSTRUCTIONS_403 SS2 calls for: EX_A/EX_B/EX_C become real terms -- `<http://example/a>` (ldpy's own bare-IRI notation, terms.md) instead of the string `"<http://example/a>"`. Same spelling, minus the quotes; the type changes from str to URIRef. That single change is why this is 'minor-restructuring' rather than 'directly-expressible': the query line itself (`s{ ASK { {EX_A} {EX_B} {EX_C} . } }`) is a direct, unmodified substitution, but it is only correct once the supporting constants are turned into terms.

the region's own EX_A/EX_B/EX_C (now URIRef) are decoupled from starlight_shim.py's private _EX_A/_EX_B/_EX_C (kept as the original pre-formatted strings, needed verbatim by _graph_with_one_fact's N-Triples `g.parse(data=f"...", format="nt")`): the shim is shared, identical, and unaware of how the region chooses to spell its own copies.
`bool(s{ ASK { ... } })` replaces `qres.askAnswer is True` -- querying.md gives this exact form (`assert bool(s{ ASK { ex:a a ex:Sensor } })`) and it is equivalent to askAnswer for a well-formed ASK.

@graph g designates the existing graph returned by _graph_with_one_fact(), following current-graph.md's 'designate: no new graph' form -- no @prefix needed since the query uses only bare IRIs, no prefixed names.

repair.driver: pilote écrit à la main (run_pair ne peut pas changer le graphe que le test reçoit) : il exécute les deux artefacts, puis, pour douze graphes construits par g.parse(data=..., format="nt") comme le fait le dépôt, rebranche _graph_with_one_fact dans l'espace de noms de chaque côté et compare le résultat de l'appel (None ou l'exception, type et message) : le fait seul, entouré de triplets sans rapport, graphe vide, un voisin par terme du motif qui partage les deux autres termes avec la cible (a b d), (a x c), (z b c), les trois voisins sans puis avec la cible, les trois termes à d'autres rôles, le fait réflexif, un objet littéral "<http://example/c>" ; le pilote exige en outre que les cas discriminent (certains lèvent, d'autres non) ; docstring qui dit ce que chaque cas exerce.
mutants_killed: ASK { a b ?x } (objet élargi) ; ASK { a ?x c } ; ASK { ?x b c } (vert avant pour l'objet)
assert ask is True -> assert ask is not None ; assert retiré
EX_A remplacé par la chaîne "<http://example/a>" (littéral simple au lieu d'une IRI)
repair.remaining: Jugement non traité : le retypage de EX_A/EX_B/EX_C (str -> URIRef) modifie des constantes que le dépôt partage avec _graph_with_one_fact ; la paire reste une région de test, qui ne peut pas illustrer l'article.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: `g` and `ask` inlined into one `assert _graph_with_one_fact().query(...).askAnswer`; `is True` dropped, askAnswer being a bool.

optimized.ldpy: the ground ASK becomes `assert m{ {EX_A} {EX_B} {EX_C} }(_graph_with_one_fact())`, the existence test of m{ } (bool of its solutions); EX_A/EX_B/EX_C are IRIs in the translated header.
No exception to the symmetry rule.
header_optimization_notes: Nothing unused in either header: optimized_header.py and optimized_header.ldpy are copies of optimized.py and optimized.ldpy. The shim import and the three EX_ constants are read by the region.
